There is no evidence that these carriers will have their traffic diverted to any greater extent than other segments of the motor carrier industry as a result of our action herein. We have determined that any diversion of traffic from existing carriers which might occur will not significantly harm reliable and efficient carriers, and that any harm which might result to some carriers will be more than offset by improved motor carrier service to the shipping public. Furthermore, it would be contrary to our goals of uniformity and simplicity of regulation, and hence administratively undesirable, to exclude the traffic of certain types of motor carriers from these regulations.
This Commission shares the motor carriers' concern for safety, but this is a matter more properly considered by 63 DOT's Federal Highway Administration. No evidence has been presented which might convince us that local carriers within

The DOT will continue to supervise the safety of operations which are not subject to regulation by this Commission. The Federal Highway Administration has published (at 41 Fed. Reg. 8175 (1976)) an amendment to the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (FMCSR's) stating that in the absence of any formal proceedings by that agency to determine what effect the expansion of commercial zones may have on the safety of operations within those zones the commercial zones as referenced in the FMCSR's relating to exempt intracity operations will, for the present, be those set forth in the October 1, 1975, issue of 49 CFR 1048. The Federal Highway Administration is considering the issuance of a notice of proposed rulemaking in the near future to establish exempt intracity areas as they relate to the safe operation of vehicles in interstate commerce within the expanded zones.
